subject: ventures/business-vehicle-depreciation-calculator
professional: a CPA / enrolled agent who prepares Schedule C and 1120-S returns for small businesses with vehicle purchases; first checks: the 280F caps scaled by business use, the 6,000 lb SUV 179 limit, the 50% business-use ADS rule, and that bonus vs 179 ordering is right

evidence.correctness: Ran cli.mjs and recomputed by hand. (1) Passenger $60,000 at 100%, bonus: 20,200 / 19,600 / 11,800 / 7,060 then 1,340 residual = 60,000; matches Rev. Proc. 2025-16 caps (with-bonus 20,200; 19,600; 11,800; 7,060). OK. (2) Passenger $40,000 at 60%: bonus yr1 = 0.6 x 20,200 = 12,120, MACRS yr1 = 24,000 x 20% = 4,800 under scaled no-bonus cap 7,320. OK. (3) Exempt truck $70,000, income $50,000: 179 = 50,000 with 20,000 carryforward. OK. (4) WRONG: heavy SUV $80,000 at 90% business. Tool scales the 179 SUV cap by business use (31,300 x 0.9 = 28,170) giving year-one 179 method 36,936. Pub 946 limits the 179 deduction on the SUV to $31,300 and it is not prorated, so with basis 72,000 the 179 should be 31,300 and year one 31,300 + 20% x 40,700 = 39,440 (understated 2,504). The note text even says 'capped at $31,300 of cost' while using 28,170. Not caught by tests, which only use 100% business use for SUVs. Reading and running only, plus hand recomputation; one confirmed wrong number caps the score at 2.
evidence.completeness: README features checked: compare for passenger / heavy_suv / exempt classes (works), --json (works), --limits merge (read in cli.mjs, merges correctly), classes command (works), ADS at <=50% (works), standard mileage side-by-side (works), income limit with carryforward (works for heavy_suv and exempt; ignored for passenger, a minor gap), recapture (warning text only, not computed, disclosed). index.html and how-to page exist; 23 tests across page/usage/engine pass. Mid-quarter, leases, trade-ins, AMT, state conformity are explicitly out of scope per README. Everything claimed is present.
evidence.verification: Command: node --test '*.test.mjs' in the venture dir: 23 pass, 0 fail. Mutation 1: MACRS5 second-year 0.32 -> 0.30 in engine.mjs: 1 test failed (caught). Mutation 2 (stacked on 1): capFor year2 returned year3 cap: 2 failed (caught). engine.mjs restored from backup; git status clean; 23 pass again. Weakness: no test of heavy_suv at business use under 100%, which is exactly where the 179-cap defect lives; no test of ADS for passenger caps, no test of cap scaling for 179.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs, cli.mjs, engine.test.mjs. Small pure engine, clear applyCaps pool logic, input clamped (NaN to 0, class falls back to passenger silently), CLI validates numbers and exits 2. Defects: unknown vehicleClass silently falls back to passenger in compute(); income limit not applied to passenger class; LIMITS are year-hard-coded with a long prose string used as the as-of line; the 179 cap line uses Math.min(price, cap) * biz which is the bug above. No dead code of note.
evidence.claims: Checked: caps figures match Rev. Proc. 2025-16 and $31,300 SUV cap (backed by DEFAULT_LIMITS); 'nothing uploaded' backed by no network code in engine/cli and page; disclaimer present on README, page and CLI. Not backed: note text 'capped at $31,300 of cost' contradicts the scaled computation; page claims the 6,000 lb SUV cap 'applied' though it is applied wrongly under partial business use; llms.txt links to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host rather than marisstella.app; VENTURE stage is prototype, honest. No fake reviews.
evidence.fitness: Walk-through: a self-employed buyer of a $80,000 SUV at 90% business use (the very case in the README example) gets a Section 179 figure about $2.5k low and a tax saving figure off by about $800 at 32%; bonus and MACRS rows are right and the page tells them to confirm with a tax professional. For the common 100% business-use case, passenger and exempt results are usable and the bonus-beats-179 insight for cars is correct. Single-year placed-in-service defaults only; no 2026 limits and no mid-quarter test, so a December purchase can be wrong (disclosed).
evidence.domain: Compared against IRC 280F, 168(k), 179(b)(5) and Pub 946 chapter 5/Rev. Proc. 2025-16. Right: caps scaled by business percentage, carrying unrecovered basis forward at the later cap, ADS and no 179/bonus at <=50%, 179 limited by income. Departures: 179 SUV cap prorated (wrong); mid-quarter convention ignored (disclosed); inclusion amounts for leases, 179 for trucks over 6 ft beds not distinguished beyond user's class choice; bonus assumed 100% (correct for property acquired after Jan 19, 2025 but no switch for earlier acquisitions at 40%/60%); recapture not computed.

defects.what: Heavy-SUV Section 179 cap is scaled by business-use percent (31,300 x biz) instead of applied as an unprorated $31,300 limit on the 179 deduction; $80k at 90% shows 36,936 year one vs 39,440 per Pub 946, and the on-screen note says 31,300 while 28,170 is used
No test covers heavy_suv or 179 at business use below 100%, so the cap-scaling error passes the suite
Bonus hard-wired to 100%; no option for vehicles acquired before 2025-01-20 (40%/60% phase-down) and no mid-quarter test
llms.txt links point at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host instead of marisstella.app
Unknown vehicleClass silently becomes passenger; income limit ignored for passenger class

verdict: A small, honest, well-tested calculator whose passenger-car and exempt-truck numbers match Rev. Proc. 2025-16 and Pub 946 on three independent hand recomputations, and whose tests caught both seeded mutations (23 pass; mutants failed 1 and 2). It does not meet the bar because correctness is 2: the heavy-SUV Section 179 cap is wrongly prorated by business use, understating the 179 method by about $2.5k in the README's own example, and the tests never exercise that case. Finished as a prototype (completeness 3), but a CPA would correct the SUV row before relying on it.
